$comment: Shared locale-redirect conformance table.
An unprefixed URL cannot match a `/[lang]/…` route, so both hosts answer it
with a redirect to a prefixed one. They cannot share the code:
- crates/ruvyxa_dev_server/src/i18n.rs        (`dev`, `start`, `preview`)
- packages/ruvyxa/runtime/serverless-handler.mjs  (every serverless adapter)
They had disagreed, in two ways, and both were invisible because every test
on both sides set `detectLocale: true` and asked for an ordinary path:
1. `detectLocale: false` turned the redirect off entirely in the deployed
handler and only turned *detection* off in the native server. The
option says which signals pick the locale, not whether locale routing
happens — with it off, the native server still sent `/about` to
`/en/about` while a deployed build returned no redirect at all, so
every unprefixed URL 404ed once the project shipped.
2. The reserved namespace was excluded by raw byte prefix in the deployed
handler and by whole segment in the native server. `/__ruvyxa-notes` is
a page a project may legitimately own; it was redirected under
`ruvyxa dev` and silently excluded once deployed.
The native server's behavior is the shared one in both: it is the one that
keeps a project's URLs resolving, and the segment rule is a decision that
was already made and reasoned about there.
Every implementation replays this file:
- crates/ruvyxa_dev_server/src/i18n.rs                    (Rust test)
- tests/packages/ruvyxa/serverless-handler.test.mjs       (JavaScript test)
Add a case here first when changing what gets redirected where; a port that
drifts then fails in the language that drifted rather than in a deployed
site nobody has clicked through yet.
$knownGap: One difference is deliberately *not* settled here, because settling it is a
product decision rather than a port: the native server declines to redirect
any path that has a file extension (`Path::extension().is_some()`), while
the handler declines only paths with a known static-asset extension
(`isStaticAssetPath`). A page route such as `/docs/v1.2` is redirected by
one and not the other. No case below depends on it.
$routesNote: The page routes a case is matched against. Both replays build these two and
nothing else, so a case expecting `null` because no page exists is distinct
from one expecting `null` because the request was excluded.

cases.$why: Accept-Language matches on the primary subtag when no exact locale is offered.
Detection off still routes; it only stops the cookie and Accept-Language from being consulted. This is the case the two hosts answered differently.
A project page is not a reserved endpoint just because it shares a byte prefix with one.
The real reserved namespace still opts out.
A path that already names a locale is left alone.
Only a navigation is redirected; a POST is the request it says it is.
No prefixed page exists, so there is nothing to redirect to.
